event_definition: A new disclosure episode of explicit missed debt principal/interest payment in SEC Item 1.03 or 2.04 within (decision date, decision date + 60 calendar days]. Both items require payment-specific evidence; bankruptcy, acceleration and enforcement alone are excluded. Disclosures separated by at most 90 days belong to the same episode. Companies re-enter after more than 90 days without a qualifying disclosure, an operational quiet-gap rule rather than verified cure. Unresolved candidate filings censor their windows and later rows until reviewed. Filing date, not inferred contractual failure date, defines target timing. Negative windows require issuer filing follow-up.
sample: Eligible local companyfacts issuers with complete submissions histories and current SIC outside 6000-6999. Item 1.03 and 2.04 require payment evidence. Earlier OpenAI 2.04 PAYMENT_FAILURE/BENIGN reviews may be reused; other legacy distress and unreviewed candidates remain unresolved. Recurrent disclosure episodes are included, not only a company first-ever filing.

policy_scenario.gaps: start a new hypothetical assessment after a missing month
policy_scenario.reopening: no automatic reopening after zero within a continuous segment
policy_scenario.hard_stop: Recent known payment-failure disclosure during the configured episode quiet-gap period; no claim of contractual cure on re-entry.
policy_scenario.fallback: If no model passes the predeclared selection rule, report absence of validated improvement and use the constant training-prevalence benchmark for policy scenarios.

validation_status: Exploratory sparse-event baseline: minimum positive/negative rows relaxed from 10 to 5 and minimum event companies from 10 to 3 based on available development-period label counts. Annual tuning uses very few event companies; fitted probabilities and model selection are unstable and are not sufficient validation for operational credit decisions. Revised 2023-2025 evaluation is retrospective because earlier target results were examined.
